finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets any network client read arbitrary files the server process can read, because the user-supplied query parameter f is joined to the root with filepath.Join, which lexically resolves '..' segments, with no containment check.
finding.source: files.go:12 - r.URL.Query().Get("f"), an unauthenticated GET /dl query parameter (registered at files.go:32, listening on :8082 at files.go:34).
finding.sink: files.go:13 - os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with root = "/srv/files" (files.go:9); bytes returned to client at files.go:18.

trace.note: /dl route registered with no auth middleware
f read from query without validation
filepath.Join('/srv/files', '../../../etc/passwd') resolves to '/etc/passwd'; os.ReadFile reads it
file contents written to HTTP response

finding.guards_checked: No auth on /dl. No Clean+prefix or filepath.Rel containment check. No rejection of '..'. filepath.Join only blocks absolute-path replacement (Join('/srv/files','/etc/passwd') stays under root), which does not stop relative '..' traversal. No symlink resolution or check (EvalSymlinks absent). /avatar (files.go:22-23) checked and not reported: filepath.Base blocks traversal and '..' resolves to a directory that ReadFile rejects.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth middleware on the /dl route (files.go:32). No containment check after filepath.Join at files.go:13: no filepath.Rel, no prefix check, no rejection of "..". The filepath.Base guard at files.go:22 applies only to /avatar, not /dl.
verdict.reason: An anonymous network client can send GET /dl?f=../../../etc/passwd to the server on :8082 (files.go:34), and filepath.Join at files.go:13 resolves the ".." segments outside /srv/files before os.ReadFile reads the file and files.go:18 returns its contents, with no guard in between.
